correctness.rationale: The reduced partition Markov chain is an exact quotient of a finite absorbing voter process, with explicit transition fractions. A standard-library verifier computes every expected time from exact rational linear systems. It exhausts all connected simple graph isomorphism types through five vertices and every nonedge, giving 92 exact sign comparisons, and recomputes exact oppositely signed six-vertex edge differences. Connectedness proves eventual absorption. No finite sampling or numerical tolerance underlies the universal n<=5 exclusion.

value.rationale: Gives the exact first network size at which greater initial opinion diversity reverses whether a *specific* new social contact accelerates consensus. This structural distinction cannot be inferred from binary-only slowdown results. A complete exact census for all smaller graphs and a sharp 6-agent rational witness provide an independently reusable finite benchmark, with no inflated prediction for general social behavior.
